newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee regions to see another cold night.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee regions to see another cold night.

text.p: Brazil's meteorologists predicted another very cold night for coffee regions, with one forecasting service expecting frosts in some low-lying areas where coffee normally is not grown.

According to independent meteorologists Somar, frosts are likely to occur in lower-lying regions, particularly in the highland area of south Minas Gerais between Pocos de Caldas and Sao Sebastiao and across to Franca in Sao Paulo state.
Because of temperature inversion, dips in these areas see colder temperatures than on the slopes where coffee is generally grown.

Whether these frosts affect higher coffee-producing regions will depend on winds which are currently blowing in from the coast and which, if they continue, should protect coffee areas, said Somar meteorologist Marcos Massari.
Also recent rains have left the soil very moist which may also prevent the formation of frosts, he added.
The National Institute of Meteorology (Inmet) was also predicting a cold night in the highland region of southern Minas Gerais with temperatures falling to three degrees Celsius.
However no frosts were predicted through to Monday morning due to light cloud cover, said Inmet forecaster Manoel Rangel.
If the cloud cover opened up during Monday however, there was a risk of frosts on Monday night through to Tuesday morning, he added.
The low temperatures are due to a polar air mass which is coming in overland and therefore hitting the coffee region harder than a more humid air mass arriving from the sea.
This morning weather services reported temperatures of as low as three degrees in lower-lying regions but cooperative officials in the coolest areas said there had been no problems on coffee farms.
The air mass is expected to weigh on temperatures through to June 11, forecasters said.
